name: Owls
label: Jade Tree
lede: Cap'n Jazz minus one guitarist, back together six years later for a single Steve Albini-recorded album and one tour, then gone again for a decade.

eras.title: Cap'n Jazz, first time around
eras.text: Before Owls there was Cap'n Jazz, the Buffalo Grove, Illinois teenagers whose one album had a title longer than most of its songs. When it ended in 1995, its members scattered into The Promise Ring, Joan of Arc, American Football and more.

years.h: Toe Jam becomes [[Cap'n Jazz|04482c2e-88ab-4709-a412-85748b7ac825]] in Buffalo Grove
years.p: Brothers [[Tim Kinsella|0350b5ce-ab77-4cbf-a550-944b851e4454]] and [[Mike Kinsella|2b5e086f-cb7b-4f92-8a85-6a1c38ceb598]], [[Victor Villarreal|2758e65d-226a-4f21-b1e2-1eb72c4300b1]] and Sam Zurick start as Toe Jam. Mike Kinsella takes over drums at 12 when the first drummer quits for football.

years.h: Cap'n Jazz ends after a show in Little Rock
years.p: Cap'n Jazz breaks up after a show in Little Rock, Arkansas, the same year as its only album, known to fans as Shmap'n Shmazz. Guitarist Davey von Bohlen goes on to [[The Promise Ring|63a6fae8-d39e-4de6-bfd4-9bcbf489a565]].

years.h: Jade Tree collects Cap'n Jazz on Analphabetapolothology
years.p: The two-disc Jade Tree retrospective gathers Cap'n Jazz's recordings, demos and farewell-show tracks, and builds the audience that would be waiting for Owls.

eras.title: Civil War, then Owls
eras.text: In mid-2000 Tim Kinsella, busy leading Joan of Arc, called his old Cap'n Jazz bandmates back, all except Davey von Bohlen. They made one tangled, jazz-limbed record with Steve Albini and toured it, and then it was over.

years.h: Four ex-Cap'n Jazz members regroup as Civil War
years.p: Tim Kinsella reunites with Mike Kinsella on drums, Victor Villarreal on guitar and Sam Zurick on bass. They first play as Civil War before renaming themselves Owls.

years.h: Owls record with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] at Electrical Audio
years.p: Owls track their debut at Electrical Audio in Chicago with Steve Albini engineering. Exclaim! later noted it was made with no computers.
The label that had reissued Cap'n Jazz signs Owls, putting four Cap'n Jazz members back on Jade Tree.

years.h: Owls, the only album of the first run · Jade Tree JT1059
years.p: Math rock, jazz-like rhythms and Tim Kinsella's slippery singing. AllMusic and the Austin Chronicle gave it four stars; Stylus called it nothing special.
years.xp: Reviewers compared it to [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]], Captain Beefheart and [[American Football|4ebb5ad3-9018-407d-8c24-c03011ab9ac6]]. Germany's Ox-Fanzine hated it, calling the band terrible. The Japanese edition on Quattro added a bonus track, Later.

years.h: Mike Kinsella starts his solo project Owen
years.p: The same year as the Owls album, Mike Kinsella begins Owen, playing nearly every instrument himself and recording most of it at his mother's house.

years.h: Owls split after CMJ Music Marathon
years.p: After one tour, Owls break up following their set at New York's CMJ Music Marathon in October 2002.

years.h: Tim Kinsella and Sam Zurick start [[Make Believe|82d7935d-c121-43e3-8f33-ed999f9357f8]]
years.p: Kinsella and Zurick move on to Make Believe, while Villarreal and Zurick's instrumental band [[Ghosts and Vodka|7f7e1171-393c-4c38-b236-8e4440b83b0d]] has already come and gone.

eras.title: Two
eras.text: The Cap'n Jazz reunion opened the door, and Owls walked back through it. The second album took eighteen months to write and came out on Polyvinyl instead of Jade Tree.

years.p: Cap'n Jazz, von Bohlen included, plays the Empty Bottle in Chicago, then its first official reunion show at Louisville's Forecastle Festival on July 10.
Tim Kinsella, Mike Kinsella, Victor Villarreal and Sam Zurick start writing as Owls again, ten years after the split.

years.h: Owls finish a new record after 18 months of writing
years.p: Owls announce the follow-up to their 2001 album is complete.

years.h: Two: the second Owls album, thirteen years later
years.p: Owls release Two on Polyvinyl. The same year Mike Kinsella's [[American Football|4ebb5ad3-9018-407d-8c24-c03011ab9ac6]] reunites too.

years.h: Rolling Stone names Owls a top emo album
years.p: Rolling Stone puts the 2001 Jade Tree album Owls on its list of the 40 greatest emo albums of all time.
Tim Kinsella's main band, which he led through every lineup since 1995, breaks up.
